claims.statement: app-lynx is the repository's only runtime novel client; the former SolidJS/Capacitor webview client and its novel-reader code were deleted in ADR-0203, with the Android host moved to packages/android-host.

The /novels page renders a single-column native list (list-type=single) feed through createMixFeed with recommend/follow sub-tabs, in-flow restricted novel cards, data-layer AI-only/tag-mute removal, and navigation through the openNovel(id) seam.

Novel entry points route through the openNovel(id) seam, which applies the device-level novel_intro_first setting to emit either /novel/:id/intro or /novel/:id with no route-level redirect (ADR-0167/ADR-0183).

NovelIntro.vue is a cover-scrim decision surface whose restricted/AI masking reuses the body predicates (R18 before AI) with handler-guarded greying, and whose main CTA switches between start-reading and continue-reading labels while always navigating to /novel/:id.
The intro page builds a narrower export snapshot using caption text and an empty image map because it does not prefetch the novel body.
Novel bookmark and watch-later actions are available from both the intro page and the body page after the object-bound dimension refactor, using BookmarkButton with target-kind=novel.

NovelDetail.vue loads detail first and fetches body text/images only for non-restricted, non-AI novels, with a loadGeneration gate discarding stale responses and restricted novels bypassing the body list entirely.

The novel body is virtualized with a native list (list-type=single) of per-paragraph list-items using stable p-idx keys and estimated heights, plus meta/end/fab-allowance items; ADR-0134 measured deep-scroll jank and memory improvements from this change.

Reading progress uses the main-thread scroll signal via main-thread-bindscroll for the watchlist prompt's ≥70% signal and scrolltolower as the authoritative bottom signal, with a visible warn fallback when the MT signal does not dispatch.

NovelDetail.vue records a session-last continue-reading position on entry and evaluates completion via decideNovelCompletion at bottom, after chapter-coordinate backfill, and after a re-pulled viewport size (ADR-0219).

Lynx text selection requires static selection attribute literals, a native clipboard module (there is no navigator/clipboard), and UTF-16 code-unit index snapping; createTextSelection.ts owns event parsing, measurement, placement, dismissal, and copy/search with no optimistic copy success.

The lynx translation stack is a from-scratch BYOK feature (no shared package and no webview reuse) built on a provider-agnostic TranslationProvider whose single OpenAIResponsesProvider maps the OpenAI Responses API events to five TranslationChunk types.

The LLM API key is stored in Android Keystore via the Java PictelioTranslateModule and never enters the JS heap; JS only receives the LlmEndpointPublic mirror, and stream delivery uses the pictelioTranslateFrame global event bus with streamId/seq dedup rather than per-chunk callbacks.

createNovelTranslator implements paragraph-boundary chunking at ≤2000 chars, a fixed worker pool (concurrency 3, or 1 on the native bridge), blank-line and [N]-anchor alignment with fallback/overflow reporting, and silent AbortSignal exit.

novelTranslateStore owns the 8-state translation machine, a generation gate and AbortController, a per-chapter in-flight map that reuses the running translation, and a displayParagraphs render source that shows original, translated, or 〔未翻译〕 placeholder text.

Translation cache entries are keyed by novelId|chapterId|targetLang|modelId|sourceHash|baseURLHash with FNV-1a hashes, an LRU cap of 200, only completed chapters written, and a dual adapter: IndexedDB in web-core dev and a native filesystem channel (cacheDir/translations plus manifest.json) in PrimJS.

Translation authorization is independent of content display: isTranslationRestricted aborts R18/R18G requests before any content leaves the device, while endpoint compatibility (dummy key) and credential verification (real key) are separate persisted states.

A retryable chunked-pipeline failure triggers one whole-batch fallback (stream=false) with 0ms backoff and isRetryingHint, and partial results render translated paragraphs plus a 〔未翻译〕 placeholder without reporting 100% progress.
@pictelio/novel-export is the zero-DOM single source of truth for the 9-format whitelist, block parsing, HTML extraction, and NovelExportPayload/task-draft construction consumed by app-lynx.

NovelExporter.java is the Java facade that serializes txt/html/md/rtf/json/fb2 inline and delegates epub/docx/pdf to NovelEpubEncoder/NovelDocxEncoder/NovelPdfEncoder, fetching images via PixivImageLoader with bytes never entering JS and outputting through GallerySaver to Downloads/Pictelio.

Novel export is a kind=novel download-queue task whose opaque payloadJson snapshots targetFormat and content switches at enqueue time, reusing the queue's persistence, resume, progress, and share capabilities.
